mainEntity.name: How long does room addition planning usually take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timeline usually starts with feasibility, then design, permitting, and construction. Simple additions can move faster, but larger projects take longer because structural engineering, city review, utility coordination, and material lead times can add weeks or months. In Denver-area neighborhoods, permitting and plan review are often the pacing item, not the framing itself. If you need the space by a certain season or school date, tell the contractor early so they can plan around permit review and inspection sequencing. The safest approach is to build in extra time for revisions and weather delays.
acceptedAnswer.description: Planning can take a few weeks for a simple addition or several months for a larger one. Design, permits, engineering, and review are usually the longest parts, not the actual build.
